identity.name: Song (state)
alt_names: Song of the Spring and Autumn period

land.text: the Shang heartland around Shangqiu, enfeoffed to a member of the defeated Shang royal house

predecessors.note: The page: 'founded soon after King Wu of Zhou conquered the Shang dynasty to establish the Zhou dynasty in 1046 BC'; the founder Weizi was the brother of the last Shang king. The Zhou dossier records the enfeoffment.

land.text: Song annexed by Qi in 286, 'with troops from Chu and Wei serving on behalf of Qi'

successors.note: The pages give no division of the land; the Qi dossier has the annexation, the Chu dossier 'Chu's share', and Cliopatria hands the land to Qi in 284 and to Chu in 247.

land.text: Chu's share of the partition 'by Qi, Chu and Wei' (King Kang page)

successors.note: Land not divided on the pages opened.

land.text: Wei's share of the partition 'by Qi, Chu and Wei'; King Kang fled to Wei

successors.note: Land not divided on the pages opened.

capitals.name: Shangqiu
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Shangqiu (商丘)'; the page names no other seat.

rulers.name: Duke Xiang of Song (Zifu)
rulers.note: Text 'who reigned from 651 to 637'; the page's list gives 650-637.

rulers.name: Dai Ticheng (Lord Ticheng)
rulers.note: Ruler list 369-329; the text says 'In 355, Dai Ticheng ... ' (excerpt cut) and the King Kang page that Ticheng was killed in 328.

rulers.name: King Kang of Song (Dai Yan)
rulers.note: 'In 328 BC, he killed Lord Ticheng and seized the throne'; declared himself king in 328 on the Song page, in 318 on the King Kang page; fled to Wei in 286 and died there.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape carried back to the enfeoffment, capital Shangqiu

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's first Song shape: the enfeoffment of 1046 with the capital at Shangqiu, which lies inside the 750 bounding box (114.3-117.7E, 34.1-35.7N). The 750 shape carried back; the page gives no boundary or area for the early state.

22,623 km2 around Shangqiu for -750..-488 (the shape runs to -481; 487-481 is the new keyframe song_-487). The page gives no area (no infobox area), so there is no sanity check; the capital Shangqiu is inside.

correction.text: Song plus Cao's land around Dingtao, 'covered roughly the area of modern-day Dingtao County' (about 4,000 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 487-481: 'the State of Cao was exterminated in 487 BC after the capture of Duke Fei of Cao'; Duke Jing of Song attacked Cao ('As a result, Duke Jing of Song attacked Cao'). The page never says 'conquered by Song' or what became of the land, but Song is the attacker and the neighbour, and the Cao dossier (cao.json) reads the land as Song's from 487. Cliopatria keeps Cao as a separate state to -451 and gives Song only 2 of its cells.

correction.text: Song's 480 shape plus the Cao land annexed in 487

keyframe_review.note: 27,523 km2: Cliopatria adds 26 cells in 480, 24 of them from the western edge of Lu and 2 from Cao (page silent on the Lu land; lu.json, written by another agent, also records the 24 cells as page-silent). The correction adds Cao's whole land, annexed in 487, and keeps the Lu cells as unverified. Years -480..-451.

correction.text: Song's shape of 450 with Cao's land (annexed 487) added and Teng's cells (annihilated only in 297) removed

keyframe_review.note: 34,045 km2: Cliopatria adds 35 cells in 450, 20 from its own Xu row and 15 from its Teng row (both end in 451 there). The Teng page says Teng survived until Song annihilated it in 297, so the 15 Teng cells are taken out until 297; the 20 Xu cells (an Xu extinguished in 512 on the Xu page) stay as unverified, with Cao added.

correction.text: Song's shape of 404 with Cao's land (annexed 487) added and Teng's cells (annihilated only in 297) removed

keyframe_review.note: 34,072 km2: one cell exchanged with Lu and Qi (page silent). Same edits as song_-450: Cao's land added, Teng's cells removed until 297. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Song's shape of 383 with Cao's land (annexed 487) added and Teng's cells (annihilated only in 297) removed

keyframe_review.note: 34,200 km2: unchanged from 404 in cells. Same edits as song_-450 (Cao added, Teng removed until 297). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: Song's shape of 366 with Cao's land (annexed 487) added and Teng's cells (annihilated only in 297) removed

keyframe_review.note: 34,601 km2: Cliopatria adds 3 cells from Zheng's last shape (Zheng ends in -367 there). Page silent. Same edits as song_-450.

correction.text: Song's shape of 350 with Cao's land (annexed 487) added and Teng's cells (annihilated only in 297) removed

keyframe_review.note: 34,727 km2 for -350..-298; no Song border is dated in this period on the pages opened. Same edits as song_-450, until the annexation of Teng in 297 (song_-297).

union.text: Teng: Cliopatria's shape plus the capital Tengzhou

correction.text: Song with Teng's land (Tengzhou) annexed in 297 and Cao's annexed in 487

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for -297..-286: 'Finally it was annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC' (Teng page; the Spring and Autumn table: 'Teng 297 BCE to Song'). Cliopatria's Song shape does not grow in 297. The shape is Cliopatria's 291 shape plus Teng's land and Cao's.

union.text: Teng: Cliopatria's shape plus the capital Tengzhou

correction.text: as song_-297; the last year is 286, not 285

keyframe_review.note: 34,727 km2, -291..-285 in Cliopatria: same cells as 350. Superseded by song_-297 (the union with Teng); the state ends in 286, the year the pages give, so Cliopatria's last year (-285) is one year too long.

region.text: Shangqiu and its plain, the Song of the Shang descendants

ledger.note: 1046: the Zhou enfeoff the Shang royal house at Shangqiu and the state of Song begins. 'The state was founded soon after King Wu of Zhou conquered the Shang dynasty to establish the Zhou dynasty in 1046 BC'; infobox 'Established: 11th century BC'. The page names the capital, Shangqiu, not a boundary.

region.text: Cao's land, 'roughly the area of modern-day Dingtao County'

ledger.note: 487: Song annexes Cao. 'the State of Cao was exterminated in 487 BC after the capture of Duke Fei of Cao'; 'Duke Fei ... betrayed the State of Jin by invading the State of Song. As a result, Duke Jing of Song attacked Cao.' The page does not say Song took the land; the reading follows the Cao dossier and Song's position as the neighbour.
480: Cliopatria adds 24 cells of Lu's western edge to Song. Page silent: the Song page names no gain from Lu; the Lu dossier records the matching loss as page-silent as well.

region.text: 20 cells of the former Xu shape between Song and Lu

ledger.note: 450: Cliopatria adds 20 cells of its Xu row to Song. Page silent: the Xu page ends Xu in 512 (Wu), so the land was not Xu's in 450; counterpart 'nobody' follows that page. The 15 Teng cells that Cliopatria also adds are not taken (the Teng page has Teng alive to 297).

region.text: one cell on the Lu frontier

ledger.note: 404: Cliopatria passes one cell of Lu to Song. Page silent.

region.text: one cell on the Qi frontier

ledger.note: 404: Cliopatria passes one cell of Song to Qi. Page silent.
366: Cliopatria adds 3 cells from Zheng's last shape. Page silent.

328: Dai Yan kills Lord Ticheng, takes the throne and styles himself King Kang of Song; the ducal house of Zi gives way to the Dai. 'In 328, Dai Yan, a younger brother of Ticheng, took the throne and declared himself to be King Kang of Song'; the King Kang page dates the royal title to 318 and the seizure to 328. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Teng, in the south of modern Shandong, 'its territory corresponds to present-day Tengzhou'

ledger.note: 297: King Kang of Song annihilates Teng. 'Finally it was annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC'; Spring and Autumn table 'Teng: 297 BCE to Song'; the Song page: Song 'annexed Teng' (undated).

union.text: Teng: Cliopatria's shape plus the capital Tengzhou

ledger.note: 286: Qi, with Chu and Wei, destroys Song and the land is partitioned. 'It was conquered by the state of Qi in 286 BC'; 'the kingdom was finally annexed by Qi in 286, with troops from Chu and Wei serving on behalf of Qi'; the King Kang page: 'Song was partitioned by Qi, Chu and Wei'; King Kang fled to Wei and died there. Cliopatria's last Song year is -285.

wars.name: Song's war with Chu and the Battle of the Hong River
wars.outcome: 'The Song forces were defeated at the battle of Hong in 638'; Duke Xiang's reign ends in 637 on the page's list.
wars.note: The Hong page was not opened; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Jin-Chu campaign for Song and Cao (Chengpu)
wars.outcome: 'After Jin defeated Chu at the Battle of Chengpu in 632 BC, Jin crushed the State of Cao, rescued the State of Song'; Song's border was unchanged.
wars.note: The page says 'When Chu attacked Song, Jin made a diversionary attack on Cao', undated apart from Chengpu.

wars.name: Song's annexation of Cao
wars.outcome: Duke Jing of Song attacked Cao; Cao was exterminated in 487 and Jin sent no troops to rescue it.

wars.name: Song's annihilation of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng, a vassal of Lu and nominally conquered by Yue in 414, was annihilated by King Kang of Song.

wars.name: Qi, Chu and Wei conquest of Song
wars.outcome: King Min of Qi 'plotted with the states of Chu and Wei for a joint expedition against Song'; Song was partitioned by Qi, Chu and Wei; King Kang fled to Wei. Qin declined to intervene (Song page).
wars.note: The King Min page: 'In 286 BC, King Min attacked and destroyed Song'; Qi then 'lost all the territory it had gained' (no year).

certainty.note: The ancient frontiers of the Song plain are drawn from city territories (Dingtao, Tengzhou, Shangqiu); no treaty or survey lines exist.

notes: One dossier for Cliopatria's 'Song' (-750..-285). Wikidata Q7462 is shared with Northern Song and Southern Song (960-1279 CE), which are a different dynasty; the Song of this dossier is the Zhou-vassal state of the Shang descendants, 1046-286 BC: not merged. Cliopatria differences: (1) Cao is never added to Song in Cliopatria although Song destroyed it in 487 (Cao dossier agrees); (2) Cliopatria moves 24 Lu cells (480), 20 Xu and 15 Teng cells (450) and 3 Zheng cells (366) to Song, all page-silent; the Teng cells are removed because Teng lived to 297; (3) Teng's annexation in 297 is not drawn by Cliopatria; (4) Cliopatria's last year -285 is one year after the 286 the pages give. Unsettled: the division of the 286 partition among Qi, Chu and Wei (no page opened divides the land; Cliopatria gives Qi in 284 and Chu in 247); the Song page's 328 against the King Kang page's 318 for the royal title; the ruler table's Ticheng 369-329 against the text's 355. Pages not opened: Hong River battle, Zheng-Song wars, Xue. The page budget (5) was exceeded by two pages (Spring and Autumn, Warring States), the latter nearly empty for Song.
